scope: Exact retrospective field consequences of certified mod-2 independence; no rank or point search.
hypothesis: Exceptional directions can share a smaller joint halving extension despite their certified mod-2 independence.
panel: All 91 main-panel observations. Fields use only the specified independent witness subgroup, not every supplied point or the unknown full Mordell-Weil group.
finite_module_checks: Enumerate all 1024 normalized maps S3 to F2^2 for 1-cocycles, all 16 endomorphisms, and all subspaces of (F2^2)^r for r=1,2,3. Count common fixed-point tuples in the three affine groups of orders 24,96,384.
quartic_selection: For each of the three pinned high/low pairs: first generic point on each fibre and first selected exceptional point on the high fibre. Nine quartics total.
quartic_checks: Exact point membership, halving quartic, resolvent identity, and first good primes at most 1999 exhibiting cycle types (4) and (1,3).
limits: No number-field compositum construction, number-field discriminant computation, class group, global polynomial Galois computation, parameter sweep, or new point.
interpretation: Consequences of known class incidence, not a point-blind incidence or solubility selector. The same Galois theorem applies to insoluble Selmer classes.
legacy_boundary: Do not convert free quotient ranks in the three older MW12 embeddings to field degrees without an ambient mod-2 independence certificate.
